en.title: Week 9
now: 🧍 Stands alone · still learning sit-to-stand
🛒 Walks fast with the push walker or one hand
🧗 Climbs stairs and playground stuff, up and down
🏊 Swims since June · dips under 1–2 s
🧱 Stacks 2 blocks · uses a spoon
🖊️ Uses the pointer pen on her music book
🚪 Opens/closes closets, the toy faucet · copies adults
👏 Copies clapping and bye-bye
👉 Points + calls out to ask, very confidently
🗣️ baba/mama faded since pointing took off
✋ “Mine!” Won’t give things up without agreeing
🍽️ Wants what we eat · bigger chunks · less milk
🥛 Whole milk since Nov 3 · no open cup yet
🎒 Goes to daycare · still mouths things
en.oneLiner: One year old and very much her own person. This week, three things: turn her points into words (name it, pause, give it anyway), play her way up from the floor, and start a tiny open cup. Plus a new reading rhythm: short and often.

bigThree.title: Turn her points into words
lines: When: every time she points and calls out. Aim for 10 good moments a day: meals, bath, getting dressed, books.

How: ① Name it, short: “Banana.” ② Pause 5–10 seconds, looking at her, for any sound, look, or sign. ③ Then give it, even if she only points. Never hold it back until she says a word: pressure makes talking harder, and meltdowns don’t teach.
Two choices: hold up two things: “Apple or banana?” A point or a sound is her answer: “Banana! Here’s banana.”
Three power words: say “more,” “open,” “help” many times a day, with the MORE sign (see Baby signs). Give a little at a time so “more” has a reason.
Expand, don’t quiz: she says “ba” → “Ball! Big ball.” Not “Say ball!” Mandarin, English, or both: each person speaks their own language.

Gently, for later: her early baba/mama faded once pointing took off. That’s common, but mention it at her next checkup (CDC: tell the doctor about any skill that fades). Keep a two-week log of sounds, signs, and words to bring.

refs.label: ASHA: communication at 13–18 months
Speech Sisters (SLP parent tips)

bigThree.title: Up from the floor: sit-to-stand play
lines: When: two short floor sessions a day, when she’s fresh (after nap, before dinner).
How 1, half-kneel: she kneels at the couch; put a toy on the cushion just out of reach. She brings one foot forward and pushes up. Next time, the other leg leads.

How 2, lap-to-stand: she sits on your lap facing the couch, feet flat on the floor. A light hand on her hips, lean her body slightly forward, and she stands; then sits back onto your lap. Repeat 5 times.
How 3, squat: once she’s up, put toys at knee height, then on the floor, so she squats and comes back up.
Steps: stand her at a sturdy stool, kneel 2–3 steps away with open arms, and let her come. Hold one hand at most, not both arms up high.
Say: “Up… you did it!” If she plops: “Plop! Again?” Calm, no big fuss either way.

refs.label: Pathways.org: sit-to-stand activity

bigThree.title: First open-cup sips
lines: When: at 1–2 meals a day, sitting in her high chair. Start with water.
How: a tiny cup (shot-glass size), 1–2 sips of water in it. Hold it with her, both hands on the cup, bring it to her lip, tip slowly, let her take a sip, then set it down together.
Next: after a few days, let her hold it with your hand just under. Spills are practice: keep a towel close, no fuss.
Say: “Sip… sip. You did it!” Spill: “Oops, water fell. Wipe!”
Milk: whole milk in her cup or straw cup at meals is fine; keep it to about 16 oz/day. She’s eating more family food, so less milk is OK (see Milk at one).

cards.title: Where she is now: body
lines: She stands alone, climbs stairs and playground equipment up and down, walks fast with the push walker or one hand, and dips underwater calmly. That’s a strong, brave mover.
The missing piece is getting up from sitting with nothing to hold. It often comes around 13–14 months, sometimes after first steps, so she isn’t behind.
Heading toward (next 3 months): a few steps alone, squatting to pick things up, getting on and off the couch, then early running. Anywhere up to ~18 months for walking alone is normal.

cards.title: Where she is now: hands and thinking
lines: She stacks 2 blocks, uses a spoon, and taps a pointer pen to make music: she already knows touching a spot makes something happen (cause and effect). Those are 15-month skills.
She loves figuring out how things work (doors, faucets, lids) and doesn’t love sitting and listening. So: short, hands-on, and let her lead.
Next: 3–4 block towers, scribbling, a simple shape sorter, fill-and-dump, real helping jobs.

cards.title: Where she is now: words and understanding
cards.sub: Understands much more than she says
lines: She can: point to ask, clap and wave when you do, understand familiar names (Mama, milk, ball), simple routines (“bath time”), and often “give me” with your hand out.
Not yet: “wait,” “later,” “gently,” reasons, or “don’t” (she hears the action word). So say what TO do: “Feet on the floor,” not “Don’t climb.”

Words often pause while a big motor skill takes off; pointing has become her main tool. Coming next: trying 1–2 words or word-bits (“ba” for ball counts) by ~15 months, and pointing to show you things, not just to ask.

refs.label: CDC: milestones by 15 months

cards.title: Where she is now: feelings and self
lines: She won’t let you take something unless she agrees. That’s her sense of self growing: “This is mine, and I get a say.” It’s a good sign.
Asking first is the right instinct. See What to say for the exact words (ask, trade, warn-and-count, two choices).
Coming next: more “no,” more big feelings, showing you things she likes, and checking you’re near while she explores. The whole family uses the same simple rules (see Our family’s way).

cards.title: Eating: family food, chunks, and spitting out
lines: She wants what you eat and likes bigger pieces: great. Offer soft long strips she can bite; quarter round foods; always seated and watched.
Holding beef or sardines in her mouth for minutes, then spitting them out, is normal oral exploration: she’s learning texture and how to move food around.
Do: eat together, chew big and slow so she can see, say “chomp, chomp.” Don’t: fish it out, praise or scold the spit. Stay neutral. Tell the doctor if she gags often or swallows almost nothing.

cards.title: Reading: short and often
lines: Keep the calm 1–2 bedtime books. Add 2–3 tiny reading moments in the day (2–5 min): after nap, after breakfast, in the basket corner.
She leads: she picks the book, turns the pages (backward is fine), and stops when she’s done. Reading three pages counts.
Read with her, not to her: point and name, add sound effects (“woof!”), pause 5 seconds for her point or sound, then expand it: she points at the dog → “Yes, a big dog! Woof!”
Repeat favorites again and again; that’s how words stick. Use her pointer-pen book the same way: name, pause, then press.
Good books now: lift-the-flap, touch-and-feel, one picture per page, real-photo first-words books, and repetitive rhythm books like Brown Bear, Brown Bear and Dear Zoo.
Songs count as reading: Itsy Bitsy Spider, Pat-a-Cake, Chinese finger rhymes (手指谣), always with the motions.

refs.label: Reach Out and Read: reading with babies and toddlers

cards.title: Mouthing at daycare
lines: Mouthing is still how she explores, and she’s teething. It fades slowly through the second year.
Ask the teacher how they handle it: toys cleaned daily, nothing smaller than a toilet-paper tube opening, no button batteries or loose magnets.
At home: a yes-to-mouth basket, and swap rather than grab.

refs.label: AAP/HealthyChildren: Choking prevention

cards.title: Where the stage is heading
lines: Body: first steps alone, squat and stand, on and off the couch, early running.
Hands: towers of 3–4, scribbles, using things the right way (cup, spoon, toy phone).
Words: a few words or word-bits, then 3+ by 18 months; much more understanding.
Self: more “no” and “mine,” more pride (“I did it!”), more wanting to help with real jobs.

refs.label: ZERO TO THREE: Year 2, 13–24 months

daily: 👉 Answer her points: name it, pause 5–10 s, then give it
🔁 Say “more,” “open,” “help” in real moments
🧸 Sit-to-stand play, twice (half-kneel, lap-to-stand, squat)
🥛 Tiny open cup: 1–2 sips of water at a meal, with help
📚 2–3 short reading moments + calm 1–2 bedtime books
🤟 EAT, MILK, ALL DONE, MORE, saying the word each time
🤝 Ask or trade before taking something from her hand
🍽️ Eat together, chew slowly where she can see
🦷 Swap, don’t grab, when she mouths
Brush teeth twice (rice-grain smear)
todos: Get a tiny cup (shot-glass size or a small open cup)
Book basket: 3–5 board books face-out, low, where she plays
Start a 2-week log of sounds, signs, and words for the checkup
Write checkup questions: faded words, length, iron, milk amount
Show daycare teachers the MORE sign; ask how they handle mouthing
Make an “Open? Help?” clear jar with a favorite toy inside

quiz.q: She points at the water bottle. You wait until she says “wa” before handing it over.
quiz.why: Name it, pause, then give it anyway. Holding it hostage adds pressure and meltdowns.

quiz.q: She points at the dog in the book. You say “Yes, a big dog! Woof!”
quiz.why: You named it, added a word and a sound: that’s how words grow.

quiz.q: She’s clutching a spoon you need. You pull it out of her hand.
quiz.why: Ask or trade first. Take right away only when it’s unsafe, then offer a safe yes.

quiz.q: She holds meat in her mouth, then spits it out. You stay calm and keep eating.
quiz.why: Normal mouth exploration. Neutral, and show her how you chew.

quiz.q: Read a long story to the end even when she climbs off your lap.
quiz.why: Short and often wins. Stop when she’s done; come back later.

quiz.q: Lean her body slightly forward as she pushes up from sitting.
quiz.why: Weight over her feet is the move she’s learning. Light hands at the hips only.

quiz.q: Give her a big sippy cup of milk to carry around all day.
quiz.why: Milk at meals and snacks, about 16 oz/day. Water in the tiny open cup for practice.

scripts.when: She won’t let go of something

steps.do: Ask, and wait for her answer.
steps.say: Can I have a turn? (可以给我玩一下吗？)

steps.do: If she says no, respect it.
steps.say: Okay, when you’re done, give it to me.
You hold the lid, I’ll take the keys.
In a moment it’s Mama’s turn… one, two… thank you!
Put it in the basket, or Mama helps?

steps.do: If she’s upset, name it and hold the limit.
steps.say: You wanted to keep it. You’re mad. It’s okay to be mad.

scripts.note: Only take it straight away if it’s dangerous, then offer a safe yes: “Not this. You can have this.” Family rule, every time: dirty = OK; dangerous = remove calmly; crying = comfort, then something new.

steps.say: Banana.
(wait)

steps.do: Give it, and say it again.
steps.say: Banana! Here’s banana.

scripts.note: Even if she only points: give it. Words come with no pressure.

scripts.when: She holds food in her mouth, then spits it out

steps.say: All done with that one? Okay.
Mama chews… chomp, chomp.

scripts.note: No fishing it out, no praise or scolding. Offer again another day.

scripts.when: She grabs the book and turns pages before you finish

steps.say: Oh, you turned it! What’s here?
A duck! Quack… (wait)

scripts.note: The story isn’t the point; the talking is.

scripts.when: Something not-OK goes in her mouth

steps.say: Can Mama have that?
Not for mouths. This one is for mouths!

scripts.note: No chasing; it turns into a game.

details.title: Why words can fade when pointing takes off
lines: Babies often focus on one big skill at a time. Pointing works so well that words can take a back seat for a few weeks.
Pointing is a strong predictor of later words, especially when adults name what she points at.

Still, any lost skill is worth mentioning calmly to the pediatrician, who may suggest a quick developmental screening. A free early-intervention evaluation can be requested by parents directly in most US states.

refs.label: ASHA: communication at 13–18 months
CDC: milestones by 15 months

details.title: Why sit-to-stand comes late
lines: Standing up in open space means shifting weight forward over her feet from a crouch, with nothing to pull on. Many babies take first steps before they can do it. Either order is fine.

refs.label: Pathways.org: sit-to-stand

details.title: Why she holds food then spits it out
lines: Moving a chunk around her mouth teaches her tongue and jaw what to do with new textures. Many toddlers ‘taste-test’ like this for weeks. Neutral repetition is what helps.

signs.title: 🤟 Baby signs
signs.hint: Comes back every week. Tick the tracker when she watches, tries, or uses a sign.
signs.trackLabel: Tracker (saved on this phone, carries to next week)
signs.intro: Keep EAT, ALL DONE, MILK, and add one: MORE. She’s pointing to ask, and MORE gives that point a sign. Just say “open” and “help” for now; their signs can come once MORE sticks. Show the daycare teachers MORE too.

items.name: EAT
lines: How: fingertips and thumb pinched together (like holding a bit of food), tap them to your lips.
When: right before you offer food (“Time to eat!”) and while she eats (“You’re eating banana”).
On her body: now and then, gently bring her hand to her own mouth as you say “eat.”

images.alt: EAT sign: 1, fingertips pinched to the thumb near the mouth; 2, they tap the lips twice.
images.caption: ① Pinch fingertips to thumb → ② tap your lips twice.

items.name: ALL DONE
lines: How: both hands up, palms facing you, then twist so palms face out, like shaking something off.
When: end of every meal, bath, and play session. When she turns away or starts throwing food: “All done?” + sign.
On her body: sometimes gently twist her hands with yours, then end the activity right away so the sign means something.

images.alt: ALL DONE sign: 1, both hands up, palms facing you (others see the backs); 2, twist both wrists so the palms face out.
images.caption: ① Both hands up, palms facing you → ② twist so palms face out.

items.name: MILK
items.sub: Every cup of milk (and the bedtime bottle)
lines: How: one hand in a loose fist, squeeze open and closed twice, like milking a cow.
When: right as you hold up her cup or bottle: “Milk? Here’s your milk.” Formula or whole milk, same sign: it’s all milk.
Why this one now: she’s moving to whole milk in a cup, and she already reaches and points for it. A sign gives that point a word.

images.alt: MILK sign: 1, hand in a loose C shape; 2, squeeze into a fist, open again, twice.
images.caption: ① Loose “C” hand → ② squeeze into a fist, twice.

items.name: MORE
lines: How: both hands pinched (fingertips to thumb), tap the fingertips together twice.
When: give a little at a time (two pieces of banana, three bubbles), pause, then: “More?” + sign. Any reach or sound counts → give more right away.
Why now: she points to request all day. MORE is the most useful first “asking” sign, and it works at meals and in play.

images.alt: MORE sign: 1, both hands pinched, fingertips to thumbs, apart; 2, the fingertips tap together, twice.
images.caption: ① Pinch both hands → ② tap the fingertips together, twice.

cards.title: How to teach it
lines: Always say the word while you sign. The sign supports talking; it doesn’t replace it.
Sign on her hand or body sometimes, not only in the air: tap her lips for eat, twist her hands for all done.
Everyone does it the same way: Melody, Dad, grandparents, daycare. Same hand shape, same moments.
Celebrate any rough version. A clap, a hand wave near her mouth counts. Respond like she said it: “All done! Okay!” and act on it.

cards.title: What to expect
lines: Most babies make a first sign after weeks to a couple of months of steady modeling, often around 12–15 months.
Early signs look rough: a hand to the face for eat, flapping hands for all done. That counts.
Signing doesn’t delay speech. A randomized trial found no delay (and no big speed-up either). The real win: she can tell you “done” before she can say it, so fewer meltdowns and less food flying.

refs.label: Kirk et al. 2013, Child Development (randomized trial): baby signing did not delay or speed up speech
Fitzpatrick et al. 2014, systematic review of baby signs

timeline.footer: Many walk at 12–15 months; 16–18 is still normal. Ask the pediatrician if she isn’t walking alone by ~18 months.

By ~15 months: no new word attempts at all (word-bits count)
Doesn’t understand “give me” or simple routines by ~15 months

plays.name: Couch to Mama
plays.how: Couch to you, 2–3 steps. Kneel with open arms instead of holding both her hands; let her lean and fall into you. (Wk 4, harder)

plays.name: One-hand walk
plays.how: She walks with one hand now. Keep your hand at her shoulder or lower, swap sides, end on one finger. (Wk 4, harder)

plays.name: Playground mission
plays.how: Pick ONE stretch per visit (a new climber, a bigger slide with you at the bottom). Stop while she’s happy. (Wk 1)

plays.name: Bring-it delivery, 2 steps
plays.how: “Pick up the ball and give it to Grandma.” Help with a gesture. (Wk 1, harder)

plays.name: Point-and-name walk
plays.how: Carry or walk her around: “Where’s the light?” When she points, look and name it. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Pen-book turns
plays.how: She taps a picture; you name it and pause before the music plays. Add one word: “Cat! Soft cat.” Then her turn. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Echo-and-add
plays.how: Any sound counts: she says “ba” while pointing → “Ball! Big ball.” Add one word, never “say ball.” (Wk 3)

plays.name: Family photo book
plays.how: “Where’s Nainai? Where’s Yeye?” Pat the photos; grandparents are far away now, so this keeps them close. (Wk 4)

plays.name: Quiet board book
plays.how: Lift-the-flap or real-photo book. She turns the pages; you point, name, pause 5 s for her point or sound. Stop when she wanders off. (Wk 1)

plays.name: Banana or cracker?
plays.how: Hold up two things. Any reach, look or point is her answer: name it. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Three-cup shuffle
plays.how: Hide a toy under one of three cups and move it while she watches. (Wk 3, harder)

plays.name: Stack & crash
plays.how: Aim for 3, then 4 blocks: you build 2, hand her the third. Crash and cheer. (Wk 1, harder)

plays.name: Lid lab, harder
plays.how: Lids that pull off, then lids that push on; a box with a slot to post things through. (Wk 1, harder)

plays.name: Freeze dance
plays.how: Music on: bounce. Off: “FREEZE!” (Wk 3)

plays.name: Rhythm copy
plays.how: Tap a pot twice, wait, copy what she does. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Gesture songs
plays.how: Itsy Bitsy Spider, Pat-a-Cake, or a Chinese finger rhyme. Pause right before the motion so she fills it in. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Copy-me
plays.how: Wipe the table, phone to ear, brush hair. She copies, then you copy her. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Wipe-up helper
plays.how: Damp cloth after meals; she “cleans” her tray. (Wk 1)

plays.name: Solo play + check-ins
plays.how: 4–6 toys out, play together briefly, then “I’ll be right here.” Smile when she looks back. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Water table pouring
plays.how: Winter version at the sink or in the tub: cups, a colander, a funnel. Pour, watch it rain through. You right there, always. (Wk 4)

plays.name: Floor to stand
plays.how: Toy on the couch while she half-kneels: one foot forward, push up. Switch which leg leads. Lean her body slightly forward as she rises. (Wk 7, harder)

plays.name: Squat, pick up, stand
plays.how: Scatter 4–5 balls on a clear floor while she stands. “Can you get the red ball?” She squats, grabs, stands up. That’s the exact move she needs to stand from the floor.

plays.name: Honor her point
plays.how: She points and calls out → go there, name it, and give it if it’s OK: “Ball! You want the ball. Here’s the ball.” If not OK: name it and offer something else.

plays.name: Toy-kitchen turns
plays.how: Her toy faucet: you turn it, then wait. Add a cup to “fill” and pour into a bowl. Name it: on, off, pour, all gone.

plays.name: In and out
plays.how: Fill-and-dump, harder: a basket she fills, pushes across the room, and dumps. All pieces wider than a toilet-paper tube. (Wk 7, harder)

plays.name: Open-cup sips
plays.how: At meals: 1–2 oz in a small open or straw cup. Hold the bottom with her, tip slowly, let her set it down. Spills are practice.

plays.name: Bath pour and blow
plays.how: Pour a cup of water slowly over the back of her head (warn first: “Water’s coming… splash!”). Blow bubbles in the water together. Keeps her swim calm about water on the face.

plays.name: Yes-to-mouth basket
plays.how: A small basket of things that are fine to chew: a silicone teether, a cold washcloth, a big wooden ring. When she mouths something unsafe, swap: “That’s not for mouths. This one is!”

plays.name: Mirror signs
plays.how: In front of a mirror: EAT, MILK, ALL DONE, and the new one, MORE. Slowly, saying each word. (Wk 7)

plays.name: Hats, socks, off and on
plays.how: Let her pull off her hat or socks, then hold them out: “Your turn, on?” Undressing comes first; it’s her first self-care.

plays.name: Find the same (step 2)
plays.how: Hold up a red ball: “Where’s another red one?” with 2 balls on the floor (red, yellow). Then try a red block next to a red ball. Still two colors. (from parent posts)

plays.name: Posting box
plays.how: Cut a slot in a formula-tin or oatmeal lid; post big lids or 2-inch wooden discs. Start with a round hole + balls, then the slot. Tilting the disc is the hard part. (Montessori “coin box”, IG favorite)

plays.name: Ball drop tube
plays.how: Tape a paper-towel or wrapping-paper tube on the wall at a slant; she drops a ball in the top and watches it come out the bottom. Use a wide poster tube and balls bigger than a toilet-paper tube opening. (IG/XHS DIY)

plays.name: Big sticker peel
plays.how: Large stickers (palm-size or bigger) on the back of your hand or her tray edge; she peels them off and sticks them on paper. Lift a corner for her at first. Supervised. (XHS 贴纸 favorite)

plays.name: Sticky wall
plays.how: Contact paper taped sticky-side out on a low wall; she sticks big paper shapes or scarves on and pulls them off. Great while standing. (IG/XHS DIY)

plays.name: Colander poking (pre-threading)
plays.how: Thick pipe cleaners or chopsticks poked into a colander’s holes; take them out, poke again. Real bead threading comes ~18 months+ with big 2-inch beads. Supervised. (IG Montessori favorite)

plays.name: Teddy goes to daycare
plays.how: Act it out with a stuffed animal: Teddy gets a hug, “Mama comes back,” waves bye-bye, plays, then Mama comes back: “I came back!” Let her be Mama.

plays.name: Bubbles: “More?”
plays.how: You blow 3 bubbles, then stop with the wand up. Look at her and wait. Any sound, reach, or a MORE sign → “More! More bubbles!” and blow. If she just points, blow anyway and say “more.” You hold the bottle. (Speech-therapist favorite, e.g. @speechsisters)

plays.name: Ready, set… GO!
plays.how: Roll a ball or a car down a cushion ramp: “Ready, set…” pause, look at her, “GO!” After a few rounds, pause longer so she can fill in “go” with a sound or a look. (Parent SLP accounts)

plays.name: “Open? Help?” jar
plays.how: Put a favorite toy or snack in a clear jar she can’t open. Hand it to her and wait. When she brings it or pushes it at you: “Open! Help, open.” Open it right away; don’t hold out for a word. (Speech-therapist tip)

plays.name: Look what I found!
plays.how: Hide 3–4 interesting things in a basket (a big pinecone, a whisk, a scarf). When she holds one up to you, react to the showing: “Oh, you’re showing me! A whisk!” Pointing to share is the next step after pointing to ask. (Montessori-parent treasure basket)

plays.name: Stacking-cup games
plays.how: One set of nesting cups, four games: hide a toy under one, nest them by size, stack a tower and knock it down, “find the red one.” About 10 min a day; when it falls, laugh, never scold. (Parent tip)

plays.name: Road to a 4-block tower
plays.how: Easiest first: drop blocks into a cup → ring stacker → soft cups or tins → big blocks. Move up only when one feels easy. Falling is part of it. (Parent tip; 3–4 block towers usually come around 15–18 months)

plays.name: Swap and swap back
plays.how: Turn-taking as a game: “Can I have a turn?” She holds out the toy (or not). You play 3 seconds, hand it right back: “Your turn!” Then offer a trade: “Spoon for the cup?” She learns giving isn’t losing. (Parent tip)

plays.name: Stool stand, then steps to you
plays.how: She stands at a small sturdy stool or the couch playing; you kneel 2–3 steps away with a toy and open arms. Coax, don’t pull: let her let go and come to you. Hold one hand at most, never both arms up high. (Parent tip)

plays.name: First scribbles
plays.how: Tape big paper to the high-chair tray or floor; one chunky egg-shaped or palm crayon. You scribble a line, then hand it over. Any mark counts. Crayon goes away when it goes in her mouth. (IG toddler-art parents)

plays.name: Shape sorter: circle only
plays.how: Cover every hole but the circle (tape), give her only round pieces. Add the square next week if it’s easy. (Montessori-parent tip)

plays.name: Socks in the basket
plays.how: Real helping job: hand her socks one by one from the laundry, she drops them in the basket. “Thank you, helper!” Also: wipe the table after meals. (@busytoddler-style real jobs)

plays.name: Nature walk basket
plays.how: Outside with a small basket: collect a big leaf, a pinecone, a stick. Name each one, feel it, smell it. Too-small things stay outside. (Reggio/forest-school parents)

plays.name: She picks the book
plays.how: 2–3 board books face-out on a low shelf or basket. Let her choose, hold it, and turn the pages (even backward). Read one page or ten; stop when she’s done. (Parent tip)

zh.title: 第9周
now: 🧍 能自己站 · 从坐到站还在学
🛒 推着学步车或牵一只手走得飞快
🧗 楼梯、游乐设施上上下下都会
🏊 六月开始游泳 · 能潜水一两秒
🧱 会摞两块积木 · 会用勺子
🖊️ 会用点读笔点书放音乐
🚪 会开关柜门、玩具水龙头 · 爱学大人
👏 会跟着拍手、拜拜
👉 指着东西“啊啊”要，特别有底气
🗣️ 会指以后，爸爸妈妈反而说得少了
✋ 手里的东西，她不同意就不给
🍽️ 想吃大人吃的 · 爱吃大块 · 奶喝得少了
🥛 11月3日开始喝全脂奶 · 还没用过敞口杯
🎒 上托班了 · 还爱往嘴里塞东西
zh.oneLiner: 满一岁了，越来越有自己的主意。这周三件事：把她的“指”变成话（说出来、等一等、照样给）、玩着练从地上站起来、开始用小敞口杯喝水。另外加一个读书的新习惯：每次短短的，一天多几次。

bigThree.title: 把她的“指”变成话
lines: 什么时候：她一边指一边叫，每次都接。一天争取好好接十次：吃饭、洗澡、穿衣服、看书。
怎么接：① 简单说出来：“香蕉。” ② 看着她等5到10秒，等她出个声、看一眼或比个手势。③ 然后就给，她光指不说也照样给。千万别“不说就不给”：一逼她更不愿开口，闹起来也学不到东西。
让她选：两样东西举起来：“苹果还是香蕉？”她指一下、哼一声就算回答：“香蕉！给你。”
三个好用的词：“还要”“打开”“帮忙”，一天说很多遍，“还要”配上手势（见宝宝手语）。东西一次少给点，她才有机会“还要”。
跟着说，别考她：她说“ba”→“球！大球。”别说“说‘球’！”。说中文、英文或者两样都说都行，每个人说自己最顺口的语言。
轻轻记一笔：她之前会叫的爸爸妈妈，会指以后说得少了。这很常见，但下次体检跟医生提一句（美国疾控中心建议：会过又不会了的本事都告诉医生）。记两周她发的音、比的手势、说的词，带去给医生看。

refs.label: 美国言语听力协会：13–18个月的交流能力（英文）
Speech Sisters（语言治疗师，Instagram，英文）

bigThree.title: 玩着练：从地上站起来
bigThree.sub: 大运动 · 一天两次，每次5分钟
lines: 什么时候：一天两次，挑她精神好的时候（睡醒后、晚饭前）。
玩法一，单膝跪：她跪在沙发前，把玩具放在沙发垫上、够不着一点点。她会一只脚往前迈、撑起来。下次换另一条腿先迈。
玩法二，从腿上站：她坐在您腿上，面朝沙发，两脚踩地。您手轻轻扶着她的胯，让她身体稍微往前倾，她就站起来了；再坐回您腿上。来五次。
玩法三，蹲下：站起来以后，把玩具先放膝盖高，再放地上，让她蹲下去拿、再站起来。
迈步：让她扶着结实的小凳子站，您蹲在两三步外张开手等她过来。最多牵一只手，别把她两只胳膊高高拎着走。
可以说：“起来……站起来啦！”坐下了：“扑通！再来？”语气平静，成不成都别大惊小怪。

refs.label: Pathways.org：从坐到站练习（英文）

bigThree.title: 开始用敞口杯喝两口
lines: 什么时候：一天一两顿饭，坐在餐椅上。先用白水。
怎么练：用一个很小的杯子（小酒杯那么大），倒一两口水。您和她一起端，两只手都扶着杯子，送到她嘴边，慢慢倾，让她喝一小口，再一起放下。
过几天：让她自己端，您的手在下面虚托着。洒了就是在练，旁边放块毛巾，别着急。
可以说：“喝一口……真棒，自己喝的！”洒了：“哎呀，水掉了，擦一擦！”
喝奶：吃饭时用杯子或吸管杯喝全脂奶没问题，一天大约480毫升（16盎司）就够。她饭吃得多了，奶少点没关系（见一岁转牛奶）。

cards.title: 她现在：身体
lines: 能自己站，楼梯和游乐设施上上下下，推学步车或牵一只手走得飞快，潜水也不慌。大运动又强又勇敢。
还差一步：不扶东西从坐着站起来。很多宝宝13–14个月左右才会，有的先会走才会这个，所以她一点都不晚。
接下来三个月：自己走几步、蹲下捡东西再站起来、自己上下沙发，然后开始小跑。18个月之前会自己走都正常。

cards.title: 她现在：小手和脑子
lines: 会摞两块积木、会用勺子、会拿点读笔点出音乐：她已经明白点一下就会有反应（因果关系）。这些都是15个月的本事。
她最爱琢磨东西怎么弄（门、水龙头、盖子），不爱坐着听。所以：时间短、动手玩、让她带头。
接下来：搭三四块积木、乱涂乱画、简单的形状盒、装了倒、帮着做点真家务。

cards.title: 她现在：说话和听懂
lines: 她能：指着要东西，您拍手挥手她跟着做，听得懂熟悉的名字（妈妈、奶、球）、简单的日常（“洗澡啦”），您伸手说“给我”她常常会给。
还听不懂：“等一下”“待会儿”“轻一点”、讲道理、“不要……”（她只听进去后面那个动作）。所以要说该做什么：“脚踩地上”，别说“不许爬”。
大运动突飞猛进时，说话常常会停一停；现在“指”是她最好用的工具。接下来：15个月左右试着说一两个词或半个词（“ba”就是球，算数），还会指给您看东西，不光是指着要。

refs.label: 美国疾控中心：15个月里程碑（英文）

cards.title: 她现在：情绪和“我”
lines: 手里的东西，她不同意您就拿不走。这是自我意识在长：“这是我的，我说了算。”是好兆头。
先问她，这个直觉是对的。具体怎么说，见下面怎么说（问一问、换一换、数一数、两个都行的选择）。
接下来：会更多说“不”、情绪更大，会拿东西给您看，玩着玩着回头确认您在不在。全家用同样简单的规矩（见家庭教养原则）。

cards.title: 吃饭：吃大人的饭、爱大块、含着再吐
lines: 想吃大人吃的、爱吃大块，很好。给软软的长条让她自己咬；圆的东西切成四瓣；一定坐着吃、大人看着。
牛肉、沙丁鱼含在嘴里好几分钟再吐出来，是正常的口腔探索：她在学怎么对付新口感、舌头怎么搬运食物。
要：一起吃，大口慢慢嚼给她看，说“嚼嚼嚼”。别：伸手抠出来，也别夸或说她吐。表情平平的就好。如果常常干呕，或者几乎什么都不咽，就告诉医生。

cards.title: 读书：每次短一点，次数多一点
lines: 睡前一两本照旧，安安静静的。白天再加两三次小读书，每次两到五分钟：睡醒后、早饭后、书篮边上。
她做主：她挑书、她翻页（倒着翻也行），她不想看就停。读三页也算读了。
陪她读，不是读给她听：指着说名字，加点声音（“汪汪！”），停5秒等她指或发音，再帮她说长一点：她指着狗 →“对，大狗狗！汪汪！”
喜欢的书反复读，词就是这么记住的。点读书也一样：先说名字，停一停，再点。
现在适合的书：翻翻书、触摸书、一页一个图、实物照片认知书，还有重复句式的书，比如《棕色的熊，棕色的熊》《亲爱的动物园》。
唱儿歌也算读书：《小蜘蛛》、拍拍手、各种手指谣，都要配上动作。

refs.label: Reach Out and Read：和小宝宝一起读书（英文）

cards.title: 在托班啃东西
lines: 往嘴里放东西还是她探索的方式，加上在长牙。一岁到两岁会慢慢少。
问问老师怎么处理：玩具每天消毒，比卫生纸筒口小的东西不放在宝宝能拿到的地方，没有纽扣电池和散落的小磁铁。
在家：准备一篮“可以啃的”，看到她啃不该啃的就换，别硬抢。

refs.label: 美国儿科学会：预防噎呛（英文）

cards.title: 接下来会怎样
lines: 身体：自己迈出第一步，蹲下再站起，上下沙发，开始小跑。
小手：搭三四块，乱涂乱画，东西会“正确地”用（杯子、勺子、玩具电话）。
说话：先有几个词或半个词，18个月左右三个以上；听懂的会多很多。
自我：更多“不要”“我的”，更多得意（“我做到了！”），更想帮大人干活。

refs.label: ZERO TO THREE：宝宝第二年，13–24个月（英文PDF）

daily: 👉 接住她的“指”：说出来、等5–10秒、再给她
🔁 在真实场景里说“还要”“打开”“帮忙”
🧸 从坐到站的小游戏，两次（单膝跪、从腿上站、蹲下捡）
🥛 小敞口杯：吃饭时喝一两口水，大人帮着
📚 白天两三次小读书 + 睡前安静读一两本
🤟 比“吃”“奶”“吃完了”“还要”，边比边说
🤝 要拿她手里的东西，先问或者换
🍽️ 一起吃饭，慢慢嚼给她看
🦷 她啃了不该啃的，换，别抢
刷牙两次（米粒大小的牙膏）
todos: 买个小杯子（小酒杯大小或小敞口杯）
弄个书篮：三到五本纸板书，封面朝外，放在她玩的地方
开始记两周：她发的音、比的手势、说的词，体检带去
写下体检要问的：说的词变少了、身长、补铁、奶量
把“还要”的手势比给托班老师看；问问他们怎么处理啃东西
准备一个“打开？帮忙？”透明罐，里面放她喜欢的玩具

quiz.q: 她指着水杯，您非等她说出“水”才给。
quiz.why: 说出来、等一等，然后照样给。拿东西“要挟”她只会更有压力、更容易闹。

quiz.q: 她指着书上的狗，您说：“对，大狗狗！汪汪！”
quiz.why: 说了名字，又加了一个词和声音，词就是这么长出来的。

quiz.q: 她手里攥着您要用的勺子，您直接抽走。
quiz.why: 先问或者换。只有危险的东西才马上拿走，再给她一个能玩的。

quiz.q: 她把肉含在嘴里，最后吐了，您不动声色继续吃。
quiz.why: 正常的口腔探索。表情平平的，嚼给她看就好。

quiz.q: 她从腿上爬走了，您还坚持把长故事读完。
quiz.why: 短一点、多几次更好。她不想看就停，过会儿再读。

quiz.q: 她从坐着往上撑时，扶着她身体稍微往前倾。
quiz.why: 把重心移到脚上，正是她在学的动作。手只轻轻扶胯。

quiz.q: 给她一大杯牛奶，让她拿着走来走去喝一天。
quiz.why: 奶在正餐和点心时喝，一天大约480毫升。小敞口杯用白水练。

steps.say: 可以给我玩一下吗？
好，等你玩完再给我。
你拿着盖子，妈妈拿钥匙，好不好？
等一下轮到妈妈哦……一、二……谢谢你！

steps.do: 或者给两个都行的选择。
steps.say: 放进篮子里，还是妈妈帮你放？

steps.do: 她不高兴了，说出她的感受，规矩不变。
steps.say: 你还想玩，生气了。生气没关系。

scripts.note: 只有危险的东西才马上拿走，然后马上给一个能玩的：“这个不行，这个可以。”全家统一：脏了没关系；危险的每次都平静地拿走；哭了先抱抱，再换个新玩意。

steps.say: 香蕉。
（等一等）
香蕉！给你香蕉。

scripts.note: 她光指不说也给。没有压力，话才会来。

scripts.when: 她把食物含半天又吐出来

steps.say: 这块不吃啦？好。
妈妈嚼嚼嚼……

scripts.note: 别抠，别夸也别说她。改天再给。

scripts.when: 书还没读完，她抢过去自己翻

steps.say: 哦，你翻过来啦！这是什么？
小鸭子！嘎嘎……（等她）

scripts.note: 重点不是讲完故事，而是一来一往地“聊”。

scripts.when: 她把不能吃的东西放进嘴里

steps.say: 给妈妈好吗？
这个不能放嘴里，这个可以！

scripts.note: 别追着抢，不然她会当成游戏。

details.title: 为什么会指了，说的反而少了
lines: 宝宝常常一阵子专攻一样大本事。“指”太好用了，说话就可能先放一放，过几周再回来。
会指，是以后说话的好苗头，尤其是大人能接住、说出她指的东西。
不过，会过又不会了的本事，都值得心平气和地跟儿科医生提一下，医生可能建议做个简单的发育筛查。在美国大多数州，家长也可以自己申请免费的早期干预评估。

refs.label: 美国言语听力协会：13–18个月的交流能力（英文）
美国疾控中心：15个月里程碑（英文）

details.title: 为什么“从坐到站”学得晚
lines: 不扶东西站起来，要从蹲着把重心往前移到脚上，手上没有可以借力的地方。很多宝宝先会走才会这个，哪个先都正常。

refs.label: Pathways.org：从坐到站（英文）

details.title: 为什么含着再吐出来
lines: 把一块食物在嘴里挪来挪去，是在教舌头和下巴怎么对付新口感。很多宝宝会这样“试吃”好几周。大人淡定、多给几次，最管用。

signs.title: 🤟 宝宝手语
signs.hint: 每周都有。她看着您比、自己试着比、真的会用，就在下面打个勾。
signs.trackLabel: 进度（存在这台手机上，下周接着用）
signs.intro: “吃”“吃完了”“奶”接着比，再加一个：“还要”。她整天指着要东西，“还要”正好给她的“指”配个手势。“打开”“帮忙”这周先说，等“还要”比顺了再加手势。也比给托班老师看看。

items.name: 吃
items.sub: 给她吃东西前、吃的时候
lines: 怎么比：五个指尖捏在一起（像捏着一小口饭），往嘴唇上点一点。
什么时候比：端饭给她之前（“要吃饭啦！”），她吃的时候（“在吃香蕉呢”）。
在她身上比：时不时轻轻握着她的小手，碰碰她自己的嘴，嘴里说“吃”。

images.alt: “吃”的手语：1. 五指指尖捏到一起，靠近嘴边；2. 在嘴唇上点两下。
images.caption: ① 指尖捏拢 → ② 往嘴唇上点两下

items.name: 吃完了 / 不要了
lines: 怎么比：两只手举起来，手心朝自己，再一翻，手心朝外，像把东西甩掉。
什么时候比：每顿饭、每次洗澡、每段游戏结束时都比。她扭头不吃、开始扔饭时，问一句“吃完了吗？”同时比。
在她身上比：偶尔握着她的小手一起翻，然后马上结束，让她知道这个手势真管用。

images.alt: “吃完了”的手语：1. 两手举起，手心朝自己（别人看到的是手背）；2. 手腕一翻，手心朝外。
images.caption: ① 两手举起，手心朝自己 → ② 手腕一翻，手心朝外

items.name: 奶
items.sub: 每次喝奶（包括睡前那瓶）
lines: 怎么比：一只手半握拳，捏紧、松开，捏两下，像挤牛奶。
什么时候比：把杯子或奶瓶举到她面前时：“要喝奶吗？给你。”配方奶、牛奶都比这个，都是“奶”。
为什么现在加：她正在换杯子喝牛奶，本来就会伸手、指着要。比个手势，她的“指”就有了名字。

images.alt: “奶”的手语：1. 手半握成C形；2. 捏成拳再松开，两下。
images.caption: ① 手半握成C形 → ② 捏紧、松开，两下

items.name: 还要
lines: 怎么比：两只手都捏成一撮（指尖碰拇指），两手指尖对着碰两下。
什么时候比：一次少给一点（两块香蕉、三个泡泡），停一下，再问：“还要吗？”同时比。她伸手、出声都算 → 马上再给。
为什么现在加：她一天到晚指着要东西。“还要”是最好用的第一个“要东西”的手势，吃饭玩耍都用得上。

images.alt: “还要”的手语：1. 两手捏成一撮，分开；2. 两手指尖对碰两下。
images.caption: ① 两手捏成一撮 → ② 指尖对碰两下

cards.title: 怎么教
lines: 比手势时嘴里一定要说出来。手语是帮她说话的，不是代替说话。
时不时在她身上比，别光在空中比：“吃”就点点她的嘴，“吃完了”就握着她的小手翻一翻。
全家比法一样：妈妈、爸爸、爷爷奶奶、托班老师，同样的手势，同样的时候用。
比得歪歪扭扭也要鼓励。手往脸上一拍、两手乱挥都算。像她真说了一样回应：“吃完啦！好！”然后照做。

cards.title: 心里有个数
lines: 大多数宝宝要天天看、看上几周到一两个月，才比出第一个，常在12–15个月左右。
刚开始比得不像：手往脸上一碰就是“吃”，两手乱甩就是“吃完了”，这些都算数。
教手语不会让说话变晚。随机对照研究发现不会耽误说话（也不会让说话明显变早）。真正的好处是：她还不会说之前就能告诉您“不要了”，哭闹和扔饭都会少一些。

refs.label: Kirk 等 2013，《儿童发展》随机对照研究：教宝宝手语不会让说话变晚，也不会变早（英文）
Fitzpatrick 等 2014，宝宝手语系统综述（英文）

timeline.hint: 每一步可能要几天到几周，也可能跳着来。

steps.label: 不知不觉站住
steps.note: 玩着玩着就松手了（会了）

steps.label: 不扶东西从地上站起来
steps.note: 手撑地、屁股撅起、往上推（正在练）

steps.label: 走比爬多
steps.note: 脚分得开、手举着、老摔，都正常

steps.label: 走得稳
steps.note: 能拿着东西走、转弯、蹲下

ruler.label: 健康宝宝第一次独立走路的时间（世卫组织）：

timeline.footer: 很多宝宝12–15个月会走，16–18个月也正常。18个月左右还不能自己走，就问问儿科医生。

watch: 会的本事退步了：不指了、不挥手、不咿呀、叫名字不回头
15个月左右还完全不试着说词（半个词也算）
15个月左右还听不懂“给我”或简单的日常指令
吃饭常常干呕、噎着，或者几乎什么都不咽
噎住了：咳不出、哭不出、喘不上气、发紫 → 马上打911，同时拍背/压胸
吞了纽扣电池或磁铁，看着没事也要马上去急诊
发烧38°C以上，而且精神很差

ZERO TO THREE：宝宝第二年（英文PDF）

plays.name: 从腿上走到沙发
plays.how: 沙发到您怀里，两三步。您蹲着张开手等，别牵她两只手，让她自己往前倒、扑过来。（第4周，升级）

plays.name: 牵一只手走
plays.how: 她已经能牵一只手走了。手不高过她肩，左右换，最后只给一根手指。（第4周，升级）

plays.name: 游乐场小挑战
plays.how: 每次只挑一样新的试试（新的攀爬架、大一点的滑梯，您在下面接）。她还开心时就收。别抱着她一起滑。（第4周）

plays.name: 帮忙送东西
plays.how: “把球拿起来，给奶奶。”配上手势帮她听懂。（第4周）

plays.name: 指一指，说一说
plays.how: 抱着或牵着她转转：“灯在哪儿？在这儿！”她指什么，您就看过去说出来。（第4周）

plays.name: 点读书轮流玩
plays.how: 她点一个图，您先说名字，停一下再让音乐响。多加一个词：“猫！软软的猫。”再轮到她。（第3周）

plays.name: 跟着说再多一点
plays.how: 她发什么音都算：指着说“ba”→“球！大球。”加一个词就行，别让她“说球”。（第3周）

plays.name: 翻家庭相册
plays.how: “奶奶在哪儿？爷爷在哪儿？”拍拍照片。爷爷奶奶回国了，翻翻相册让她记着。（第4周）

plays.name: 安静读绘本
plays.how: 翻翻书或实物照片书。她自己翻，您指着说名字，停5秒等她指或发音。她走开就结束。（第1周）

plays.name: 香蕉还是饼干？
plays.how: 两样东西举起来让她选，她看哪个、指哪个都算回答，您说出来。（第4周）

plays.name: 三个杯子藏玩具
plays.how: 玩具藏在三个杯子中的一个下面，当着她的面挪一挪，让她找。（第4周）

plays.name: 搭了推倒
plays.how: 目标三块、四块：您先搭两块，递给她第三块。推倒了一起欢呼。（第1周，升级）

plays.name: 开盖子、投进去
plays.how: 能拔开、能按上的盖子；盒子开个口，让她把东西塞进去。她弄不开时先等一等。（第4周）

plays.name: 木头人跳舞
plays.how: 音乐响就晃，一停就“定住！”（第4周）

plays.name: 学节奏
plays.how: 敲锅两下，等等她，她怎么敲您就怎么学。（第4周）

plays.name: 手指谣
plays.how: 《小蜘蛛》《拍拍手》或者手指谣（“一个手指点点点”）。做动作前停一下，等她接。（第3周）

plays.name: 跟我学
plays.how: 擦桌子、打电话、梳头，她学您，您再学她。（第4周）

plays.name: 一起擦桌子
plays.how: 吃完饭给她一块湿布，让她自己“擦”餐盘。擦不干净没关系。（第4周）

plays.name: 自己玩，大人在旁边
plays.how: 摆出四五样玩具，先陪玩一会儿，再说“奶奶就在这儿”，坐远一点看着。她回头看您时笑一笑。（第4周）

plays.name: 玩水桌倒水
plays.how: 冬天就在水池边或澡盆里玩：杯子、漏勺、漏斗。倒水、看水从洞里“下雨”。大人一直在旁边。（第4周）

plays.name: 从地上站起来
plays.how: 她单膝跪着时把玩具放沙发上：一只脚往前迈、撑起来。换条腿来。她起身时扶着让身体稍微往前倾。（第7周，升级）

plays.name: 蹲下捡、再站起来
plays.how: 她站着的时候，地上撒四五个球：“把红球捡起来？”蹲下、抓、站起来，正是从地上站起来要练的那个动作。

plays.name: 她指，您就接
plays.how: 她一边指一边“啊啊”叫，您就走过去，说出来，能给就给：“球！你要球呀，给你。”不能给：说出来，再换个能玩的。

plays.name: 玩具厨房轮流玩
plays.how: 玩具水龙头：您拧一下，停下来等她。再给个杯子“接水”，倒进碗里。边玩边说：开、关、倒、没啦。

plays.name: 放进去、倒出来
plays.how: 装了倒，升级：她把小篮子装满、推着走、再倒出来。东西都要比卫生纸筒粗。（第7周，升级）

plays.name: 小杯子喝两口
plays.how: 吃饭时小敞口杯或吸管杯倒一两口（30–60毫升）。您托着杯底一起端，慢慢倾，让她自己放下。洒了就是在练。

plays.name: 洗澡倒水、吹泡泡
plays.how: 先说一声“水来啦……哗！”再用杯子慢慢从后脑勺浇。一起在水里吹泡泡。让她对水扑到脸上保持淡定，跟游泳课接上。

plays.name: 可以啃的小篮子
plays.how: 放几样可以啃的：硅胶牙胶、冰过的湿毛巾、大木环。她啃了不能啃的，就换：“这个不能放嘴里，这个可以！”

plays.name: 对着镜子比手语
plays.how: 对着镜子比：吃、奶、吃完了，再加新的“还要”。慢慢比，边比边说。（第7周）

plays.name: 帽子袜子，脱了再戴
plays.how: 让她自己扯掉帽子、袜子，再递给她：“你来戴？”先会脱再会穿，这是她最早的自理。

plays.name: 找一样的（第二步）
plays.how: 举起红球：“另一个红的在哪儿？”地上只摆一红一黄。再试试红积木放红球旁边。还是只用两种颜色。（家长分享的玩法）

plays.name: 投币盒
plays.how: 奶粉罐或燕麦罐盖子上开个口，投大瓶盖或5厘米的大木片。先开圆洞投球，再换成长缝。把木片转过来对准缝，是最难的一步。（蒙氏投币盒，Instagram上很火）

plays.name: 滚球管道
plays.how: 把粗纸筒（海报筒）斜着贴在墙上，她从上面放球，看球从下面滚出来。球要比卫生纸筒口大。（Instagram、小红书都有人做）

plays.name: 撕大贴纸
plays.how: 手掌大的贴纸贴在您手背或餐盘边上，她撕下来贴到纸上。一开始帮她翘起一个角。大人在旁边看着。（小红书很火的贴纸游戏）

plays.name: 粘粘墙
plays.how: 矮处墙上贴一张透明贴纸（粘面朝外），让她把大纸片、丝巾粘上去再撕下来。站着玩，还顺便练站。（Instagram、小红书DIY）

plays.name: 插漏勺（穿珠前练习）
plays.how: 粗扭扭棒或筷子插进漏勺的小洞，拔出来再插。真正穿珠子要18个月以后，用5厘米大珠子。大人看着。（Instagram蒙氏常见）

plays.name: 小熊上托班
plays.how: 拿个毛绒玩具演一遍：抱一抱，“妈妈会回来”，挥手拜拜，小熊在托班玩，妈妈回来了：“我回来啦！”换她来当妈妈。

plays.name: 吹泡泡：“还要吗？”
plays.how: 吹三个泡泡就停，举着泡泡棒看着她等一等。她出个声、伸手、比“还要”，您就：“还要！还要泡泡！”接着吹。她光指也照样吹，嘴里说“还要”。泡泡水大人拿着。（语言治疗师常用的玩法）

plays.name: 预备……走！
plays.how: 球或小车从靠垫斜坡上滚下去：“预备……”停一下，看着她，“走！”玩几轮后停久一点，让她用声音或眼神来接“走”。（家长和语言治疗师常用）

plays.name: “打开？帮忙？”透明罐
plays.how: 把她喜欢的玩具或零食放进她打不开的透明罐子，递给她，等一等。她拿过来塞给您，您就说：“打开！帮你打开。”马上打开，别非等她说出来。（语言治疗师的小技巧）

plays.name: 百宝篮：“看我找到啥！”
plays.how: 篮子里放三四样好玩的东西（大松果、打蛋器、丝巾）。她举起来给您看时，接住她的“给您看”：“哦，给妈妈看呀！打蛋器！”指给别人看，是“指着要”之后的下一步。（蒙氏家长的百宝篮）

plays.name: 套杯四种玩法
plays.how: 一套套杯，玩四样：扣住藏玩具、按大小套进去、摞高再推倒、“红的在哪儿”。一天十分钟左右。倒了就笑，千万别说她。（家长分享的玩法）

plays.name: 一步步搭到四块
plays.how: 从简单的来：积木丢进杯子 → 套圈 → 软杯子或铁罐摞 → 大积木。这一步玩得轻松了再往下走。倒了很正常。（家长分享；搭三四块一般在15–18个月左右）

plays.name: 换过来、再换回去
plays.how: 把轮流变成游戏：“可以给我玩一下吗？”她给（或不给）都行。您玩三秒，马上还给她：“轮到你啦！”再试试交换：“勺子换杯子好不好？”让她知道给出去不等于没了。（家长分享）

plays.name: 扶凳子站，再朝您走
plays.how: 她扶着结实的小凳子或沙发站着玩，您蹲在两三步外，拿着玩具张开手。逗她过来，别拉：让她自己松手走过来。最多牵一只手，别把她两只胳膊高高拎起来。（家长分享）

plays.name: 第一次涂鸦
plays.how: 大纸贴在餐椅托盘上或地上，给一支粗粗的蛋形蜡笔。您先画一道，再递给她。画出什么都算。放进嘴里就收起来。（Instagram 幼儿美术家长）

plays.name: 形状盒：只留圆洞
plays.how: 其他洞用胶带贴住，只留圆洞，只给圆的块。玩得轻松了，下周再开方洞。（蒙氏家长的做法）

plays.name: 袜子放进篮子
plays.how: 真正的小家务：收衣服时把袜子一只只递给她，让她丢进篮子。“谢谢小帮手！”吃完饭一起擦桌子也算。（Instagram 上很多家长这么做）

plays.name: 散步捡宝贝
plays.how: 带个小篮子出门，捡大叶子、松果、小树枝。一样样说名字，摸摸、闻闻。太小的不带回家。（瑞吉欧、森林学校家长的做法）

plays.name: 她自己挑书
plays.how: 两三本纸板书封面朝外放在矮书架或篮子里。让她自己挑、自己拿、自己翻（倒着翻也行）。读一页还是十页都行，她不想看了就停。（家长分享）
